title: Obtain a finite sector-changing response without a free two-level projection
statement: In the actual linear-profile canonical contact, a nonnegative finite eta waveform with area A satisfies A^2/64<=P(+to-)<=K_*A^2 when A*sqrt(2K_*)<=1 and t<=hbar/(16lambda Y_*), for the declared prepared-plus joint-state reference moment bounds.

requires: Linear -lambda*YQ full-ladder Hamiltonian, supplied J+ joint preparation with actual reference Y and D moments, finite eta waveform/control and a compatible sector-sensitive instrument.
provides: In the actual linear-profile canonical contact, a nonnegative finite eta waveform with area A satisfies A^2/64<=P(+to-)<=K_*A^2 when A*sqrt(2K_*)<=1 and t<=hbar/(16lambda Y_*), for the declared prepared-plus joint-state reference moment bounds.
assumptions: No automatic application to nonlinear finite-aperture w_L. No unbounded-D norm, free Gaussian bath, unique NESS, joint eta,T remainder or cold heat law. The optional uniform actual-Y work estimate has an extra no-bound-pole/finite-L1 free-response contract.
costs: Actual offset peak/slew, source work and preparation/detection/reset; finite moment/time gates. Source-reported finite-matrix diagnostics are not replayed.
contract.units: A dimensionless, t time, eta dimensionless offset, D charge number and Y position; transition probability is dimensionless.
contract.obstruction: Exact static degeneracy and a dipole are insufficient; the proved output here is a conditional finite-clock response, not persistent cold transport.

body: Retain D=-sigma_x tensor d and Q=I tensor T+sigma_z tensor P0, or consistently use the rephased alternative. The positive full-sector B=DC spectrum retains all modes. Compare actual evolution to exp(i*a(t)D)U0 by state-induced Duhamel; the defect is bounded by the actual Y reference moment rather than an invented bounded D norm. Half-integer |D|>=1/2, its actual D^2 moment and Markov bound give the finite transition lower bound. Preparation, sector-sensitive readout and independent copies are real premises. The fixed-(T,t) eta expansion and moment bounds do not identify cold infrared weight.
